We are profoundly saddened to learn of the sudden passing of a true Manhig Yisrael. Rabbi Moshe Hauer zt"l was a dear friend and respected colleague whose unwavering devotion to the Jewish people and to Torah was exemplary and impactful.
 
We extend our deepest condolences to his family and to our partners in the Orthodox Union. May his memory be a blessing and his legacy continue to illuminate the path of Am Yisrael.

After attending President Trump’s address to the Knesset, Rabbi Dr. Ari Berman, President of Yeshiva University, spoke with Maria Bartiromo, Mornings with Maria on Fox Business about the release of the final 20 living hostages — a moment filled with both joy and reflection.
 
President Berman shared a message of gratitude and commitment, emphasizing that leadership in times of crisis means embodying faith, unity, and moral courage. His words remind us that every act of redemption, every step toward peace, carries the weight of our shared values and collective hope.
 
🎥 Watch Rabbi Berman’s complete interview here. https://www.foxbusiness.com/video/6382684462112

This fall, the Shevet Glaubach Center for Career Strategy and Professional Development hosted two major recruiting events: the Fall 2025 Tech Career Fair and the Fall 2025 Finance & Accounting Fair. 

At the Tech Career Fair, 230 students connected with top employers — including Amazon, BlackRock, Citi, Goldman Sachs, Intelligent Traffic Control, MarketAxess, MongoDB, Uveye, and PwC — to explore technical internships and full-time roles for Summer 2026. 
At the Finance & Accounting Fair, nearly 300 students engaged with 26 employers, 63 professionals, and 40 alumni, including representatives from Deloitte, EY, Goldman Sachs, Grant Thornton, J.P. Morgan, and KPMG, while exploring career paths and opportunities for Summer/Winter 2026 internships. 

A huge thank you to our students, employers, and alumni for making these events impactful. Together, we help students turn opportunities today into career steps for tomorrow.

The new Rabbi Norman Lamm Digital Archive, launched in cooperation with Yeshiva University, is now live. Rabbi Lamm, who served as YU’s third president, was a leading figure of Modern Orthodoxy. This unprecedented resource opens thousands of his sermons, lectures, essays, and letters to the public for the first time, celebrating YU’s proud heritage and making his teachings freely accessible to rabbis, educators, students, and lay leaders everywhere.

Legislators, entrepreneurs and industry experts gathered together at Wednesday night's Hack the Hate NYC event to share ideas and actionable steps towards combating antisemitism online.

Featured speakers include Shiran Mlamdovsky Somech, Founder & CEO of Generative AI for Good; Keynote Speaker Anne Neuberger, Former Deputy National Security Advisor of the United States; and panel moderators Dr. Tamar Avnet, Associate Dean and Professor of Marketing at Sy Syms; Alexandra Lebovits Benedon, Executive Board Member of the NY Israel Chamber of Commerce; and Guy Franklin, Founder & CEO, Israeli Mapped in NY. 

Video messages were shared from Leo Terrell, Senior Counsel to the Assistant Attorney General for the Civil Rights Division and Chair of the DOJ Task Force to Combat Antisemitism, and Chen Shmilo, CEO of 8200 Alumni Association. 

YU's President, Rabbi Dr. Ari Berman, delivered opening remarks and Rabbi Moshe Hauer, Executive Vice President of the Orthodox Union concluded the evening. 

The event was held at the YU Museum and was organized by Yeshiva University's Sy Syms School of Business, Generative AI for Good and 8200 Alumni Association. 

Stay tuned for the full recap article on the YU News blog site at www.yu.edu/news
